correctness.rationale: From the exact symmetric degree normalization k=1+w derive d′=−2w e^(−αd)d/(1+w), w′=w(1−w)(2e^(−αd)−1). Differentiating Ψα(d)=log d−Σ(αd)^k/(k k!) gives Ψ′=(2−e^(αd))/d; direct substitution cancels d/dt[Ψ+2atanh w] identically. Ψ rises to unique maximum at d_c=log2/α and falls beyond. Monotone d and phase-plane invariant yield exhaustive w_c=tanh[(Ψ(d_c)−Ψ(d0))/2] cases. Critical Taylor coefficient Ψ(d_c)−Ψ(d_c+z)=α z²/d_c+O(z³), w=(α/(2d_c))z²+O(z³), z′=−αz²/2(1+O(z)), hence z~2/(αt), w~2/((log2)t²). Since d0≤2, α*=(log2)/2 is sharp. Independent derivative/invariant and several numerical instances passed; those finite instances do not prove the global limit.
